subject: coal mine
title: 1,099 Miners Died in 1906. Twenty Days Later, 13 Walked Out Alive

scenes.text: Twenty days after a mine exploded, 13 men walked out.
March 1906, northern France. A blast tore through a coal mine and killed 1,099 miners.
It's still the deadliest mine disaster in European history.
Three days later, the search ended, and the missing men were declared dead.
But deep underground, 13 survivors were groping through dark, smoky tunnels, living on whatever scraps they could find.
On day twenty, with no rescue coming, they found their own way back to the surface.

description:
On 10 March 1906, an explosion at the Courrières coal mine in northern France killed 1,099 miners, Europe's deadliest mining disaster.
Twenty days later, on 30 March, a group of 13 survivors reached the surface. Their story made the regional word rescapé, survivor, famous across France.
How long do you think you could last trapped underground?
first_comment: Expert rescue teams came from Paris and Germany, but France had almost no trained mine rescuers of its own. Could you survive twenty days in total darkness?
